title: GPU fleet capacity, cloud accounts & IaC CI/CD ops runbook (2026)
author: Alex Chen
content:
Summary:
This ops guide consolidates the GPU fleet & capacity strategy, cloud account and networking conventions, Terraform/IaC module reference, and CI/CD & build practices used by infra teams when operating Redwood's inference fleet. It includes runbook playbooks for common incidents (capacity exhaustion, node OOMs, networking partitions), a concise Terraform module API reference, CI/CD gating rules, and ownership/maintenance cadence.

Scope and audience:
- Primary audience: infra engineers, SRE, platform, and eng-serving-runtime teams.
- Scope: cloud accounts (AWS primary), VPC/networking patterns, GPU node types and capacity planning, Terraform modules and usage examples, CI/CD for infra modules and GPU AMI/build pipeline, and runbook response procedures.

Table of contents:
1) Goals and SLOs
2) GPU fleet & capacity model
3) Cloud accounts & networking conventions
4) Terraform / IaC modules (reference + examples)
5) CI/CD and build pipelines (infra modules & GPU images)
6) Operational runbooks (incidents + scaling)
7) Ownership, maintenance cadence, and onboarding checklist
8) References and related pages

1) Goals and SLOs
- Goal: provide predictable, cost-efficient GPU inference capacity with 99.9% availability for Dedicated and a 99% availability target for burst/hosted pools.
- Capacity SLOs and thresholds (team-level):
  - Node-level availability SLO: 99.9% (monthly).
  - Scale-up latency SLO: 95% of autoscale requests satisfied within 90s for pre-warmed pools.
  - Emergency scale-up window: < 15 minutes for manual warm-up of additional reserved pools.
  - Cost efficiency target: average $/token improvement of 20% year-over-year through quantization and batching improvements.

2) GPU fleet & capacity model
- Fleet composition (primary):
  - p4d.24xlarge + A100 80GB equivalent for large model serving (Dedicated).
  - g5.12xlarge (A10G / A100 equivalent) for mixed latency workloads.
  - spot-kick pools used for non-critical background workloads and model eval.
- Pool types and use cases:
  - Reserved (Dedicated): always-on, pinned to customer/tenant, high isolation. Autoscaling disabled by default.
  - Shared (hosted): multi-tenant, workload-aware autoscaling, strict per-tenant concurrency limits.
  - Burstable: short-duration burst capacity for spikes with graceful degradation to fallback models.
- Key metrics to monitor:
  - GPU utilization (GPU%): target 45-70% for cost efficiency, sustained >85% triggers capacity review.
  - Average queue wait time: >1s should trigger scale-up or batching config changes.
  - OOM rate per model: track per model, OOM >0.5% of requests -> revert recent model changes / adjust batch size.
- Warm pool strategy:
  - Maintain per-region warm pool capacity equal to 20% of typical peak per region (weekly rolling average).
  - Warm pools are pre-initialized with top-5 production models and a lightweight health-check endpoint.

3) Cloud accounts & networking conventions
- AWS account layout:
  - org-root: management account (billing, IAM baseline).
  - infra-prod: production infra (VPCs, fleet control-plane, router).
  - infra-staging: staging environment matching prod at 80% scale.
  - infra-dev: developer preview (limited GPU quota).
- VPC & subnet naming:
  - VPC: vpc-<region>-<env>-<purpose> (e.g. vpc-us-west-2-prod-gpu).
  - Subnets: subnet-<zone>-<tier> (e.g. subnet-usw2a-private-app).
- Networking patterns and required configs:
  - Cross-account access: use IAM role-assume with least privilege, with logging enforced by CloudTrail in management account.
  - Security groups: default deny; allow only required ports: 22 from bastion (restricted), 9090 and 9443 for metrics and control-plane only between infra subnets.
  - VPC peering / Transit Gateway: per-customer private deployments use TGW attachments scoped by account tag: "redwood:customer:<customer-id>".
- Routing & NAT: GPU nodes placed in private subnets with NAT Gateway for outbound control-plane API calls.
- Network observability:
  - Flow logs to central logging account (retention 90d).
  - Per-region NLB metrics for GPU serving endpoints with target group health thresholds: unhealthy >2 consecutive checks -> trigger node remediation.

4) Terraform / IaC modules (reference + examples)
- Naming conventions: modules live in git under infra-terraform/modules/<module-name>.
- Key modules and responsibilities:
  - module/gpu-node-pool: creates ASG/Managed node group, launch template, IAM roles, GPU drivers & AMI bootstrap.
  - module/networking-vpc: VPC, subnets, route tables, TGW attachments.
  - module/iam-role: baseline roles for node and control plane.
  - module/ami-builder: Packer + outputs of AMI IDs per region.
- Example module interface (inputs/outputs table):
  - Inputs (gpu-node-pool): region, env, instance_types (list), desired_capacity, min_capacity, max_capacity, gpu_ami_id, user_data_template.
  - Outputs: autoscaling_group_id, launch_template_id, instance_profile_arn, node_pool_tags.
- Example usage (HCL snippet):
```hcl
module "gpu_node_pool_inference" {
  source         = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood/infra-terraform.git//modules/gpu-node-pool"
  region         = "us-west-2"
  env            = "prod"
  instance_types = ["g5.12xlarge"]
  desired_capacity= 10
  min_capacity   = 5
  max_capacity   = 30
  gpu_ami_id     = data.aws_ami.redwood_gpu.id
}
```
- Terraform lifecycle and testing:
  - All module changes require: unit tests (terratest), pre-apply plan approval, and pipeline run in staging with a smoke test.
  - Committee: changes that affect networking or cross-account roles must have 2 reviewers including an SRE reviewer.

5) CI/CD and build pipelines (infra modules & GPU images)
- Repos and pipelines:
  - infra-terraform (modules and environment overlays): pipeline triggers on PR, runs fmt -> validate -> terratest -> plan. Plan artifacts stored in S3 with unique plan id.
  - infra-ami (packer): build AMI pipeline in GitHub Actions -> publish to SSM Parameter with semantic version tag.
- Pipeline gates:
  - Lint/format and static tests must pass.
  - Terratest must pass against ephemeral test account.
  - For prod-affecting changes use manual approval step with "Infra Approvers" group.
- Release process for AMIs:
  - AMI builds are immutable. Tag format: redwood-gpu-ami-<version>-<region>. Use SSM param /infra/ami/gpu/<region>/latest -> value is AMI id.
- Automated rollback policy for module deployment failures:
  - If apply fails in prod: pipeline automatically notifies #infra-ops and posts failed plan link. On approval, revert terraform to last-known-good commit and re-run apply.

6) Operational runbooks (incidents + scaling)
- Incident: sudden capacity exhaustion (high queue depth / requests failing due to no capacity)
  1) Triage: check dashboard (Grafana: GPUPoolOverview) -> key panels: queue depth, average latency, GPU utilization by pool.
  2) Assess root cause: increased traffic vs scheduled maintenance vs autoscaler failure.
  3) Immediate mitigation (ordered):
     a) Trigger manual scale-up of warm pool: run CLI job (infractl scale pool --pool <pool-id> --add 10) and set "manual_warm=true".
     b) Enable model fallback route in router config to a smaller model variant (router UI -> route -> enable fallback).
     c) If scaling not possible, toggle customer rate-limits for non-critical tenants (admin console).
  4) Post-incident: run detailed capacity runbook, update capacity model and schedule additional reserved capacity if needed.
- Incident: GPU node OOMs / frequent container restarts
  1) Identify affected ASG / launch template via CloudWatch: filter by NodeOOM alarm.
  2) Isolate: cordon nodes in k8s cluster (kubectl cordon <node>) and drain gracefully (kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data).
  3) Recreate nodes: new instances launched by ASG; if issue persists, roll the launch template to previous stable AMI/Bootscript.
  4) Mitigation: reduce per-container batch size, reduce model max_tokens, or revert recent model/container image changes.
- Incident: control-plane networking partition (nodes not reachable by control-plane)
  1) Validate TGW routes, route tables, NACLs, and security groups.
  2) Check VPC Flow Logs for drop reasons.
  3) If TGW is impacted, failover to regional control-plane endpoint (instructions: update control-plane config in SSM /infra/controlplane/<region>/endpoint -> set to regional-backup).
- Escalation and postmortem:
  - Pager escalation matrix: oncall -> infra-sre -> infra-eng lead. Contacts in rotation stored at /oncall/infra-sre/rotation.
  - Postmortem required if incident impact >4 hrs or customer SLA violated. Postmortem template: summary, timeline, root cause, mitigation, action items, owner, due date.

7) Ownership, maintenance cadence, and onboarding checklist
- Ownership:
  - GPU fleet capacity: infra-sre team (primary), eng-serving-runtime (secondary for model-related regressions).
  - Networking & cloud accounts: infra-accounts subteam.
  - Terraform modules: infra-terraform owners in CODEOWNERS.
- Maintenance cadence:
  - Weekly: capacity review slide in team sync (last-7d usage, forecast next-14d).
  - Monthly: AMI security rebuild, dependency updates, and IaC module deprecation review.
  - Quarterly: capacity planning cycle for major customer forecast changes.
- Onboarding checklist for new infra engineer:
  1) Access: grant AWS console access (infra-dev) and assume-role for infra-staging/prod.
  2) Local dev: clone infra-terraform and run make test (needs docker / terratest).
  3) Observe: review Grafana dashboards GPUPoolOverview, infra-alerts, and read recent postmortems.
  4) Shadow oncall for two rotations.

8) References and related pages
- infra-iac-and-gpu-fleet-guide-2026 (architecture & spec)
- gpu-capacity-and-infra-runbook-2026 (detailed runbook)
- infra-gpu-fleet-capacity-ci-cd-iac-playbook-2026 (playbook)
- infra-ami build repo: git@github.com:redwood/infra-ami.git

Appendix: quick commands
- Scale pool (CLI): infractl scale pool --pool <pool-id> --add 10 --region us-west-2
- Force replace launch template: terraform apply -target=module.gpu_node_pool_inference.aws_launch_template.this
- Get current AMI (SSM): aws ssm get-parameter --name "/infra/ami/gpu/us-west-2/latest" --query Parameter.Value --output text

Change history:
- 2025-10-15: created by Alex Chen (initial published).
- 2026-02-10: updated: added AMI release process and expanded CI/CD gating requirements (Samantha Liu).

Notes and next work items:
- Add automated warm-pool forecasting job (ML-based) to reduce manual scaling.
- Consolidate AMI build artifacts in centralized artifact registry with signed provenance.

For questions or reviews, contact the owner team (engineering) or reviewers listed above.
